text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 2.7% today to $154, capping a five-day rally that has lifted the stock 5.1% since late last week. The move tracks a sharp rise in global oil prices—world crude hit $123.10 per barrel today, a level not reflected in the earlier part of this two-week window—suggesting investors are pricing in tighter energy supplies. News of Qatari mediators holding talks in Tehran to potentially restart U.S.-Iran negotiations likely spooked the market into worrying that a deal could ease geopolitical tensions and increase Iranian oil exports, prompting a rush by energy traders to lock in gains before that risk materializes.

The strength also reflects real tightness in fuel markets right now: tankers are still moving oil through the Strait of Hormuz despite escalating Iranian attacks, and refining margins have surged as supplies have tightened. That backdrop means even as President Trump promised lower gas prices, the actual market conditions—tight supply, high freight costs, strong refining profits—are working in the opposite direction, benefiting major oil producers and refiners in the near term.
